currentImplementation.population: SELECTED rows with finite D5 return
currentImplementation.status: DESCRIPTIVE_READY if selectedD5Samples>=30 regardless of scenario economics

fixedSyntheticWitness.conclusion: Sufficient sample count can satisfy the cost-related governance check even when every displayed stress scenario is economically adverse.

scopeProblems: It is an equal-stock selected-name D5 stress, not portfolio-capital-weighted realized trading cost.
It uses signal/selection-date outcome returns rather than verified fills/turnover.
It tests absolute selected returns, not candidate-specific incremental alpha after costs.
Current generic outcome provenance guards also apply to the D5 returns feeding this stress.
safeInterpretation: The 30/60/100bps table is descriptive sensitivity, not proof of cost robustness.
A future Formal optimization candidate must evaluate its own incremental effect under a preregistered, evidence-backed friction model.
Do not invent a new universal pass threshold from these outcomes.
requiredRepair: Until Trading Frictions provides an evidence-backed applicable cost model, costEconomicState is UNKNOWN for promotion purposes.
When a candidate is proposed, freeze the relevant turnover/execution assumptions before outcome comparison.
Use verified fill/turnover where available; label modeled vs actual costs separately.
Governance must not treat sample-count sufficiency as completion of the cost-economics requirement.
